item.title: 9 Near-Perfect 'Far Side' Comics Starring the Nerdy Kid
item.description: One of the biggest differences between The Far Side and most other comic strips is that The Far Side doesn’t have a recurring cast of characters. Charles Schulz’s Peanuts , for example, had Charlie Brown, Linus, Lucy, Snoopy, and the rest of the gang, while Jim Davis’ Garfield has Garfield, Odie, Jon, and a handful of other recurring characters. But Gary Larson’s The Far Side , with its non-sequitur, single-panel jokes, didn’t have regular characters, or at least not really .

item.title: Vincent Price Is the Weirdest Serial Killer Ever in this '70s Cult Classic
item.description: We are 10 minutes into The Abominable Dr. Phibes , and nobody has spoken a word. Robert Fuest’s 1971 horror film is a surreal, kitsch, and intentionally funny murder-museum of a movie. But it's also dreamlike and deeply strange in a way that lingers after you've watched it.

item.title: 5 Near-Perfect Psychological Thriller Movies Streaming for Free
item.description: Psychological thrillers trigger a fight-or-flight response within a controlled environment and entertain us at the same time. Interpersonal relationships become the source of anxiety, as there’s more at stake than someone’s physical safety — their very sanity is on the line. The novelty of great psychological thrillers like Rear Window (1954), Memento (2000), or Mulholland Drive (2001) does not wear off after a first watch. There’s more to glean than suspense or twist, as catharsis is an integral part of the experience. Unfortunately, all those movies are locked up behind various streaming service subscriptions (if they're available to stream at all).

item.title: 23 Years Later, Spike's Best 'Buffy' Quote Is Still One of the Best Lines in TV History
item.description: Buffy ’s writers gave Spike some of the show’s sharpest one-liners — who could forget “Out. For. A. Walk. Bitch.”? But his best line comes in the series finale, “Chosen.” It’s the natural culmination of a character pulled between heroism and selfishness for most of his life, and it captures the complicated truth of his relationship with Buffy.

item.title: 61 Years Later, Paul's Best Dune Line Is Still the Coldest Quote in Sci-Fi History
item.description: That said, the phenomenal success of Denis Villeneuve’s Dune movies proves that the impossible is always within reach. So far, Villeneuve’s adaptation has captured the sheer scale of the books and also made some meaningful changes to the source material. This version of Paul Atreides (Timothée Chalamet) begins his journey with a hesitant vulnerability that feels more intense than in the books. This is also why his turn as a self-proclaimed messiah feels more ominous and devastating in Dune: Part Two .

item.title: 58 Years Later, Captain Kirk's Best Star Trek Quote Is the Greatest Line in Sci-Fi History
item.description: Certain lines of dialogue become so famous they almost stop belonging to the movies and TV shows that produced them. “May the Force be with you.” “I’ll be back.” “You're gonna need a bigger boat.” You don't need to know the context. The words have long since transcended their original context.

item.title: Jean-Claude Van Damme's First Action Classic is Streaming for Free
item.description: Jean-Claude Van Damme gets a bad rap. Due to when he got famous and the sorts of movies that he usually makes, JCVD often gets lumped in with other B-tier '80s action stars like Steven Seagal and Chuck Norris , which does Van Damme a disservice.

item.title: 5 Most Perfect 1980s Games That Nobody Remembers
item.description: The 1980s wasn't the decade video games were born; the origins of the medium go back a further 20 years, through the likes of Spacewar! and Pong . But it was in the 1980s that video games grew up, exploding in popularity and complexity and establishing many of their defining stars. It was the decade that gave us Mario and Zelda, Pac-Man, Final Fantasy, Prince of Persia, and SimCity. But it also gave us some much more obscure titles that have since fallen by the wayside. Here are five fantastic '80s games that might have been forgotten, but still have something to teach us.
